# Active contact area domination and a centroid-source cost bound

This is a bounded interface for the new normal-dependent endpoint
erosions. It retains the original three fibers and their original cap
budgets. It does not assert that a deepest source is a centroid, that
all contact area is small, or that general lattice families decompose
into independent triples.

## 1. Surface-area domination on actual support contacts

Let L subset K be positive convex bodies in R^d, d>=2, and let

    Z={n in S^(d-1):h_L(n)=h_K(n)}.

This set is closed. Then their surface-area measures satisfy

    (S_L restricted to Z) <= (S_K restricted to Z).          (1)

Proof. At a surface-regular boundary point x of L with normal n in Z,
one has x in L(n) subset K(n), because both support values coincide.
Thus x also belongs to boundary K. The nonregular part of boundary K
has H_(d-1) measure zero, and so does its intersection with boundary L:
the same ambient Hausdorff measure is used on both. At every remaining
point the unique outer normal of K is n, since n already supports K
there. Hence the set of regular L boundary points with normal in any
Borel E intersect Z is, up to a null set, a subset of the corresponding
regular K boundary points with normal in E intersect Z. Comparing their
H_(d-1) measures proves (1). All sets are measurable via the Borel
unique-normal map; alternatively their completed measures give the
same conclusion. No smoothness, positive curvature or polyhedrality
is assumed. QED.

For d=1 the same assertion is direct: a contacted interval endpoint
is also the endpoint of the containing interval with the same sign
normal, and each contributes H_0 mass one.

Let A,B be positive bodies, M=(A+B)/2 subset K, and take
Z={h_M=h_K}. The proved ordinary common-area theorem in
`candidate d332d092619053f4`
gives S_A wedge S_B<=S_M. Restricting and using (1) yields

    (S_A wedge S_B) restricted to Z <= S_K restricted to Z.  (2)

In d=1 all interval area measures are the sum of the two unit normal
atoms, so (2) holds directly without that theorem.

## 2. Exact source and forced-input costs at a centroid

Suppose the selected interior source y is the ordinary centroid of K.
Then its projective parameter is zero. Put

    H(n)=h_(K-y)(n)>0,
    D=d|K|=integral H dS_K,
    R=integral_Z H dS_K,                  0<=R<=D.          (3)

The exact source erosion is the homothety of K toward y. It removes
Gamma_d D to first order or more in every cap containing y. The two
one-input continuation fields of the normal-allocation source both
have value2H(n), independent of their continuous point. Consequently
their positive normal cost measures are

    mu_A=2H S_A, mu_B=2H S_B.

Section5 of
`candidate 72bbac9873894c0b`
proves that the infimum forced input cost, using actual contact-band
cutoffs and continuous endpoint allocations, is exactly

    omega(Z)=2 integral_Z H d(S_A wedge S_B) <= 2R.         (4)

The equality is an infimum in the stated family. To use any strict
inequality one first fixes a sufficiently narrow contact band, then
an approximating continuous allocation, and only then a sufficiently
small shape parameter. It is unnecessary and generally incorrect to
assume an exactly optimal continuous allocation exists.

Suppose this source has a fixed finite cap cover for all deepest base
planes, with common original row budget Q=beta M_total, and the other
bases have finite persistent slack covers. If

    (Gamma_d-beta)D > 2 beta R,                            (5)

then (4) and the exact cap-loss construction give an actual compatible
strict global normalized-depth descent. Indeed choose forced cost C
strictly below (Gamma_d-beta)D/beta. Every chosen cap loses at least
Gamma_d D in the source, and nonnegative mass in the endpoints. The
total loss is D+C, so every cap has strictly positive surplus
Gamma_d D-beta(D+C). All original covers remain unchanged under the
nested erosions. Supporting cap coincidences require no discarded
boundary mass or allocation convention in this fixed-cap argument.

In particular, if beta<Gamma_d/2 and R<=D/2, condition (5) holds.
Thus a hypothetical such bad one-witness local minimum with a centroid
source must have MORE than half of its source cone-volume weight on
active midpoint-contact normals. This is a proved contact-area
restriction, not an assertion that those normals are absent or small
in an arbitrary family.

Using only R<=D gives the weaker sufficient beta<Gamma_d/3. This
records exactly why this denominator estimate alone falls short of
the required n=1 factor1/2. The actual endpoint cap credit in the
normal-allocation row dual remains necessary in the high-contact case.
